cards.source_title: AITW #17 Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: CLAUDE.md > prompts > research > plans > implementation
cards.claim: Human effort should be weighted to the highest-leverage pipeline stages, with CLAUDE.md first and implementation last.
cards.landing: CLAUDE.md curation priority; ship plan phase review focus

cards.source_title: AITW #17 Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Use intentional compaction: actively manage and shrink your context
cards.claim: Deliberately compact context (research and plan docs as compressed state) to keep the agent focused.
cards.landing: one phase per new session; phase handoff docs

cards.source_title: AITW #17 Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Review markdown docs to catch problems BEFORE implementation
cards.claim: Humans should review the agent's research and plan documents to gain mental alignment before any code is written.
cards.landing: ship plan phase routine: draft PR 'Plan @ sha' review gate

cards.source_title: AITW #17 Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Use sub-agents for complex tasks
cards.claim: Decompose work into sub-agents with specialised prompts (find relevant files, plan, generate) rather than one monolithic prompt; sub-agents also protect the parent context (linked thread 'How not to use SubAgents').
cards.landing: .claude/agents/ library beyond the Haiku fixflow-explorer

cards.source_title: AITW #17 Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Align language and naming
cards.claim: Consistent naming across the codebase helps the agent see relationships between parts.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (same-named slice folders across runtimes already do this)

cards.source_title: AITW #17 Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Phase 1 - Research: understanding how the system works today, including filenames
cards.claim: Three-stage workflow: research (how it works today, with filenames), plan (step-by-step outline), implement (test as you go, expect surprises).
cards.landing: phase routine in ship plan section 0

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The less context you use, the better results you get.
cards.claim: Build the workflow around frequent intentional compaction, restarting with fresh context per major phase.
cards.evidence_detail: Session had 3 context restarts to stay under 40-60% usage.
cards.landing: one-phase-per-new-session rule; compaction trigger

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: 40% context usage is the sweet spot - restart before hitting limits
cards.claim: Keep context usage around 40% (40-60% range) and restart before hitting limits.
cards.evidence_detail: A number from one 3-hour session, not a benchmark.
cards.landing: a context-usage threshold in the phase routine

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: A bad part of a plan is a hundred bad lines of code.
cards.claim: Review leverage is highest on the plan, so human review effort should concentrate there.
cards.landing: ship plan review stage; Opus reviewer on plan

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Research is 100x leverage
cards.claim: Thirty minutes documenting how the codebase works saves hours of implementation thrashing; research docs act as compressed context for planning.
cards.evidence_detail: 30 min research, 400k-line codebase, feature shipped in about 3h versus 1-2 days estimated.
cards.landing: phase 0 research doc / cold-resume artifacts

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Opus for research, Sonnet for implementation
cards.claim: Route the stronger model to codebase research and planning and the cheaper model to implementation.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated in session takeaways; no cost data.
cards.landing: model/effort routing per phase stage

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Phases should mirror how you'd code manually
cards.claim: Plans split into small independently testable and shippable phases (7 phases there), with incremental commits after each green phase.
cards.landing: ship plan 40-phase decomposition and per-phase commits

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Always read the code - This isn't magic, you're still responsible
cards.claim: The human must still read the code and have domain experts review the plan; reading is not optional.
cards.landing: owner view / reviewer step

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Specialized agents: Code locator, pattern finder, analyzer
cards.claim: Research uses three specialised sub-agents (locator, pattern finder, analyzer) running on the stronger model.
cards.landing: .claude/agents/ (add pattern-finder, analyzer beside the locator)

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Voice > typing for prompts
cards.claim: Speaking prompts injects more context than typing.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious (operator habit)

cards.source_title: AITW No Vibes Allowed live coding
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: While one agent implements, another can research the next phase
cards.claim: Parallelise by researching the next phase while the current one implements.
cards.landing: phase routine sequencing

cards.source_title: AITW Ralph Wiggum under the hood
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: One-loop, one-step. Exit. Rerun.
cards.claim: Do not convince the model to work longer; bound each loop to one meaningful step, exit and rerun.
cards.evidence_detail: Conceptual demo (Next.js to-do app), explicitly not production advice.
cards.landing: outer-loop workflow script per phase

cards.source_title: AITW Ralph Wiggum under the hood
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Back pressure is your governor.
cards.claim: Tests, types and builds act as back pressure that keeps a looping agent honest.
cards.landing: CI three jobs, import-boundary contracts as backpressure

cards.source_title: AITW Ralph Wiggum under the hood
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: One bad spec line can waste tens of thousands of tokens.
cards.claim: Specs must be right before code is generated, because one bad line propagates through the whole loop.
cards.landing: plan review before implementation

cards.source_title: AITW Ralph Wiggum under the hood
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Code is disposable. Ideas, specs, and harness design carry the value.
cards.claim: Value lives in specs and harness design, so regenerate code and plans rather than patch them.
cards.landing: durable plan/spec files; saved workflows

cards.source_title: AITW Ralph Wiggum under the hood
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Context budgeting so you stay in the smart zone
cards.claim: Budget context so the loop stays in the 'smart zone' rather than drowning the model.
cards.landing: context threshold in phase routine

cards.source_title: AITW Ralph Wiggum under the hood
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Avoid when: the task truly needs long contiguous context with weak feedback
cards.claim: Loop-style autonomy suits crisp specs plus fast checks and fails when feedback is weak or per-step human review is needed.
cards.landing: phase triage: which of the 40 phases may run unattended

cards.source_title: AITW Ralph Wiggum under the hood
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Reverse mode: deriving specs first, then generating forwards
cards.claim: Derive specs from existing code first, then generate forward; plan regeneration and resets are steering tools.
cards.evidence_detail: Demo observed self-termination, resets and plan regeneration.
cards.landing: cold-resume spec derivation; knowledge store

cards.source_title: AITW Bash vs MCP - token efficient coding agent tooling
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Token efficiency isn't just about saving money - it's about preserving context space
cards.claim: Token overhead of tool definitions matters for context budget, not only cost.
cards.evidence_detail: Claude -p write-a-file: total cache creation 13225 tokens baseline vs 18957 with the Linear MCP config (about 5.7k extra).
cards.landing: MCP/tool loadout audit; always-loaded surface including CLAUDE.md

cards.source_title: AITW Bash vs MCP - token efficient coding agent tooling
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Writing your own drop-in replacements for MCP tools
cards.claim: A small CLI wrapper documented in CLAUDE.md and allowed via Bash(prefix:*) can replace an MCP server at lower token cost.
cards.evidence_detail: Side-by-side token counts, linear-cli vs Linear MCP, via a stream-json log inspector.
cards.landing: skills or scripts instead of MCP servers

cards.source_title: AITW Bash vs MCP - token efficient coding agent tooling
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Advanced tricks like .shims for forcing uv instead of python or bun instead of npm
cards.claim: Use PATH shims to force the agent onto the project's preferred tool (uv, bun) rather than correcting it in prose.
cards.evidence_detail: Listed as a trick; no numbers.
cards.landing: mechanical enforcement instead of CLAUDE.md prose; a re-open of the hooks question

cards.source_title: AITW Bash vs MCP - token efficient coding agent tooling
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Naming conventions matter more than you think.
cards.claim: Tool and command names directly affect how accurately the model uses them.
cards.landing: naming of skills, agents and scripts

cards.source_title: AITW Bash vs MCP - token efficient coding agent tooling
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Don't just blindly use MCP for everything.
cards.claim: No one-size-fits-all: MCP helps people unfamiliar with APIs but costs tokens, so pick per need.
cards.landing: tool-loadout policy

cards.source_title: AITW Context Engineering and memory deep dive
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Treat RAG, memory, and prompts as a single, unified context engineering problem.
cards.claim: All inputs (prompts, retrieval, memory, history) are one problem of assembling the final token set.
cards.landing: knowledge-store design as context assembly

cards.source_title: AITW Context Engineering and memory deep dive
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: fetch it deterministically and inject it into the context yourself
cards.claim: For information the agent always needs, inject it deterministically instead of relying on it to ask.
cards.landing: session-start injection of key facts in place of long CLAUDE.md; hooks (skipped, re-open)

cards.source_title: AITW Context Engineering and memory deep dive
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Don't try to make your agent remember everything.
cards.claim: Memory should be an engineered lossy process (Decaying Resolution Memory): recent detail, older material compressed; summarise with existing memory in view.
cards.evidence_detail: Highlight; episode 07-15 implements DRM as code.
cards.landing: knowledge-store design; journal compaction

cards.source_title: AITW Context Engineering and memory deep dive
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: semantically meaningful, human-like tools (e.g., 'check_calendar', 'search_inbox')
cards.claim: Give agents narrow, purpose-named, sandboxed tools rather than a generic retrieve_memory function.
cards.landing: purpose-named skills/scripts for the knowledge store

cards.source_title: AITW Context Engineering and memory deep dive
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Avoid solving complex, deterministic problems like timezone conversions inside a prompt.
cards.claim: Do deterministic logic in code and hand the model a normalised format.
cards.landing: scripted checks over prompt rules

cards.source_title: AITW Anthropic Post Mortem
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Use less context. I promise you, your pipelines will be more accurate.
cards.claim: Less context gives more accurate results; long-context routing degraded smaller requests in Anthropic's incident (30% of Claude Code users affected).
cards.evidence_detail: Stated by Vaibhav; the 30% figure is from Anthropic's post-mortem; Dex endorsement not shown in notes.
cards.landing: context budget rule; CLAUDE.md trim

cards.source_title: AITW Anthropic Post Mortem
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Don't be a hero, roll back
cards.claim: When something breaks after a change, roll back first and investigate later; 30 test cases is often enough for basic eval coverage.
cards.evidence_detail: Episode notes (Vaibhav and guest Aaron); Dex adoption not shown. Notes also list a Research-Plan-Implement discussion at 54:03.
cards.landing: deploy runbook; eval sizing

cards.source_title: AITW Decoding Context Engineering Lessons from Manus
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: periodically re-inject relevant information or tasks to reinforce the context
cards.claim: In long runs the model loses the goal, so re-inject goals or plans periodically (a todo or plan file read repeatedly).
cards.evidence_detail: Takeaway from the Manus paper discussion; who said it is unclear.
cards.landing: phase routine re-reading the plan at checkpoints

cards.source_title: AITW Decoding Context Engineering Lessons from Manus
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: keeping your system message consistent and placing dynamic variables at the end
cards.claim: Keep the stable prefix identical and put dynamic content last to benefit from KV/prompt caching.
cards.evidence_detail: Takeaway; no numbers in notes. The earlier Bash-vs-MCP episode shows a cache read versus cache create contrast.
cards.landing: stable CLAUDE.md prefix; workflow prompt templates

cards.source_title: AITW Git Worktrees for AI Coding Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: use multiple agents, each working in their own git worktree to brainstorm multiple solutions
cards.claim: Run several agents in separate worktrees on the same spec, then synthesise the best answer into the feature branch by judgement or another agent.
cards.evidence_detail: Whiteboard workflow; links multiclaude, vibe-kanban, conductor.
cards.landing: best-of-N workflow in a saved workflow library; this repo already runs in worktrees

cards.source_title: AITW Git Worktrees for AI Coding Agents
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: File and Spec Management, in-tree vs out of tree
cards.claim: Where specs and plans live (inside the worktree versus outside) is a design decision for parallel agents; tmux is a building block for collaborative agent workflows.
cards.landing: where docs/program evidence and plan files live relative to worktrees

cards.source_title: AITW Using CodeLayer to Build CodeLayer
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Research / Plan / Implement to ship new features to CodeLayer itself.
cards.claim: The team dogfoods the Research/Plan/Implement workflow inside CodeLayer.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: AITW Interruptible Agents
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Don't use a framework.
cards.claim: Own your agent architecture: a simple main loop checking input between steps, or threading, and the nuances you build are the agent's identity.
cards.landing: own workflow scripts rather than a framework

cards.source_title: AITW Event-driven agentic loops
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Testing becomes deterministic - replay the same event log
cards.claim: An append-only event log projected into prompt, UI and persistence lets you replay and assert deterministically.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav and guest Anders; Dex adoption not shown. Relevant to compliance auditing.
cards.landing: append-only decisions journal as audit trail

cards.source_title: AITW Agentic RAG + Context Engineering
cards.author: other
cards.quote: Every single token counts.
cards.claim: Tool-output design (relative paths, truncation notices, rg over grep, timeouts, errors removed after correction) is context engineering; sub-agents get fresh contexts and cannot spawn more.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav live build; Dex adoption not shown; a 'no recursion' sub-agent rule.
cards.landing: script output conventions for verifiers; sub-agent depth limit
